brief.subject: Landlord pays $49.75M over hidden rental pricing
brief.headline: FTC and states reach $49.75 million settlement with big rental landlord over deceptive pricing
brief.dek: A record landlord settlement, new Amazon ad-auction allegations, and a payment processor accused of trapping small businesses in contracts.
brief.lede: Progress Residential and owner Pretium Partners will pay $49.75 million to settle FTC and state charges of misleading renters about pricing. The FTC calls it its largest enforcement matter against a landlord.

sections.heading: Record landlord settlement over rent pricing
bullets: $49.75 million: what Progress Residential and Pretium Partners will pay to settle deceptive rental pricing charges.
The FTC and four states brought the case against the largest U.S. manager of single-family rental homes.
The agency calls this its biggest enforcement action ever taken against a landlord.
Renters should compare the advertised rent against the full cost before signing a lease.

sections.heading: Payment processor accused of fake savings
bullets: $600,000: what Riverside Payments, affiliate Cascade Equipment Leasing and their operators will pay to resolve FTC and Washington allegations.
Regulators say the firms falsely promised small businesses lower payment processing costs.
They also allegedly made cancelling nearly impossible despite advertising risk-free cancellation.
Family members running small shops should read cancellation terms closely before signing processing deals.

sections.heading: Amazon ad-auction case gets new details
bullets: The FTC and 22 states filed an updated, unredacted complaint against Amazon over its search advertising auction.
Regulators allege Amazon used deceptive and unfair practices to secretly push up ad prices.
The new filing points to substantial harm to advertisers, according to the FTC.

brief.seo_description: Landlord settles deceptive rent pricing charges for $49.75 million, a payment processor pays $600,000, and new details emerge in the Amazon ads case.

items.title: Progress Residential and Owner Pretium Partners to Pay $49.75 Million to Settle FTC and States’ Charges Over Deceptive Rental Pricing Practices and Other Unlawful Conduct
items.snippet: The nation’s largest property manager of single-family rental homes, Progress Residential, and its owner, private equity firm Pretium Partners, will pay $49.75 million to settle charges brought by the Federal Trade Commission and four states that the companies misled consumers with deceptive rental pricing practices.
